en.title: Longest Word Chain by Inserting One Letter
en.description:
Choose a word chain from the word list, where each next word is obtained from the previous one by inserting exactly one letter while keeping the order of the other letters. Find the number of words in the longest chain. Words of the same length cannot be predecessors of each other.

This site independently compiled the standard I/O and the solution; supplements for missing source bounds and example corrections are stated explicitly in the protocol.
en.input: The first line contains the number of words n, followed by one word per line. Original bounds 1≤n≤1000, each word has length 1..16, all lowercase English; duplicate words are allowed.
en.explanation: The outputs of the three public examples are, in order: 4; 5; 1. Checked by independent enumeration or direct simulation.
hints: Sort by length; delete each position of the current word, look up the longest chain of the resulting predecessor, and take the maximum plus 1.
